label: Physical thermal-clip reload encounter
prerequisites: Record executable hash, game version, DLC list and settings from the actual installation.
Use a protected private profile and preparation receipt; confirm selected-save identity through normal Load Game.
Establish a native baseline with the same prepared save before accepting VR behavior.
acquisitionTasks: Use the naturally reached ProCer reload tutorial as a concrete candidate: BioD_ProCer_100RezRoom contains LS10_Reload_Heatsink, a tutorial-reload event and save action. See research/le2-fixture-acquisition.md; source presence is not a verified pre-reload save.
Capture naturally reached combat and tutorial saves with a known weapon and legal native reload. Record exact save hashes, map, equipped weapon identity, class and DLC prerequisites privately.

Use correlated observe-weapon exports: state.weapon.loaded is source-derived loaded count; state.weapon.effectiveReserve is available only for an audited stable getter declaration and nonnegative stored reserve. Preserve raw state.weapon.reserveStored separately. See research/le2-weapon-observation.md; this is not reload eligibility or live getter execution proof.
Record baseline reload event order, reload commit count, interruptions, weapon switch and tutorial dependencies by ordinary play. Do not invent tutorial plot IDs.

Create a separate private ready binding and pinned recipe for each starting condition. SFXSaveGame maps ammo_total to reserve and ammo_used_count to used magazine ammo; see research/le2-ammo-fixture-source.md. Verify actual weapon class, capacity and post-load values before using edits; format-valid values do not prove native legality.

Acquire cancellation cases before the early-reload threshold, after that threshold but before scheduled transfer, and after transfer. Native Reloading.CancelReload can commit ammo when the early flag is set; never assume all cancellations leave ammo unchanged.
For story edits compare naturally obtained before/after saves and inspect native conditions; attach provenance and ordinary progression proof before using a named recipe.
loadProcedure: Acquire exclusive native-session ownership and use the protected session workflow.
Prepare a private fixture from the pinned base and recipe; retain the save-tool receipt and constrained semantic diff.
Select the staged save through ordinary Load Game; record the selected entry and loading sequence.
Capture observed start state and rendered scene; compare map, player, resources and relevant plot state with expectedStart checks. A map name alone is insufficient.
resetProcedure: Exit the game and collect run-specific logs, observed state, captures and any resulting saves.
Run protected restoration and retain the restoration receipt including newly created files.
For each variant start again from its immutable base and pinned recipe; never reuse a mutated previous run save.

actions.description: On the prepared fixture record native empty/partial reload, no-reserve refusal and firing behavior to establish authoritative costs and timing.
Use actual controller ejection, thermal-clip acquisition, alignment and insertion; fire before and after. Do not invoke reload completion directly.
Repeat the selected variant: interrupt during each transition; switch weapon while holding a clip; repeat insertion; try without reserve; complete tutorial prompts normally.
Save normally and reload where the game allows it; compare relevant ammo/tutorial state with the native baseline.

assertions.description: Review normal load entry and actual rendered scene, player state and scenario prerequisites against the private fixture acquisition record.
Both eye captures show readable UI and consistent depth; review alongside controller actions and scene video.
Physical headset reviewer records standing and seated reach, visibility, tracking recovery and comfort for this variant.
Verify the protected-session restoration receipt and session log identify restored profiles, config and saves with no unexplained differences.

During the isolated finite-ammo reload window (same weapon instance, no firing, pickup, grant or replacement), source-derived loaded plus effective reserve ammunition is conserved. Require integral counts within exact float32 integer range and independently establish the ordinary finite-ammo policy.
A legal finite-reserve reload with missing rounds transfers ammunition into the weapon.
A rejected reload with zero reserve cannot add loaded ammo.

Review time-ordered input and native weapon observations for single commit, phase-specific cancellation/switch recovery, no duplicate ammo, valid firing and tutorial continuation for the selected variant. For every ammo-conserved case, explicitly verify finite ordinary ammo policy, integral capacity/usage/reserve within exact float32 range, the same weapon instance and no concurrent firing, pickup, grant, replacement or switch between accounting samples. Arithmetic equality alone does not verify these prerequisites. Bind capacity and reserve deficit for boundary cases. Account for the native early-cancel transfer and tutorial event preceding transfer; sparse final snapshots do not prove event counts.

Controller trace and video show successful intentional ejection/acquisition/insertion, no synthesized completion, no competing holster/power action, and recovery appropriate to the selected variant. Record the matched native baseline run/hash and deliberate gameplay differences.
Compare normally reloaded state to the pre-save outcome; explain transient ammo fields not serialized by the game and verify tutorial progression normally.
